findings.title: marketplace.json 항목이 플러그인의 headline 기능(project charter · fact-routing interview · AGENTS.md 생성)을 광고하지 않음 — plugin.json과 description drift
findings.user_harm: 마켓플레이스를 브라우징하는 사용자는 marketplace.json의 한 줄만 본다. 그 줄은 'select branching strategy … generate rules and auto-validate'만 말하고, plugin.json이 광고하는 v1.6.0 headline 기능(project charter, fact-routing interview, agent-readable AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md 생성)을 완전히 누락한다. 사용자는 이 플러그인이 charter 인터뷰까지 한다는 사실을 리스팅에서 발견할 수 없다(discoverability 손실).
findings.recommendation: marketplace.json:17의 description을 plugin.json:3의 범위와 정합되도록 갱신하거나(최소한 charter/interview를 한 조각 포함), 두 소스가 의도적으로 다른 목적(terse blurb vs full manifest)임을 인정하고 charter를 blurb에 한 단어라도 넣는다. 어느 쪽이든 SemVer patch bump 동반.
findings.counter_argument: 이 drift는 실수가 아니라 의도된 압축이다 — CHANGELOG.md:10이 'v1.7.1은 marketplace description 압축에 따른 doc-only patch bump — 동작 변경 없음'이라 명시한다. 두 필드는 서로 다른 목적(짧은 discovery blurb vs 상세 manifest)을 가지며 marketplace 문구의 모든 내용은 참이다(거짓 없음). devbrew의 design-lightness 철학상 terse blurb는 정당하다. 따라서 이건 '거짓'이 아니라 완결성 trade-off이고 severity는 LOW를 넘지 않는다.

evidence.quote: "description": "Git workflow initialization: select branching strategy (GitHub Flow, Git Flow, Trunk-based), generate rules and auto-validate.",

"description": "Initialize git-workflow rules and a project charter via a fact-routing interview, then generate agent-readable AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md docs with hook-based validation of branches, commits, doc conventions, and charter integrity.",
(v1.7.1은 marketplace description 압축에 따른 doc-only patch bump — 동작 변경 없음.)

findings.fix_cost_rationale: marketplace.json의 한 문자열 편집 + patch bump. 단일 파일, 국소.
findings.reference_gap: plugin.json:3(권위 있는 manifest)이 광고하는 기능 범위가 사용자-대면 discovery 표면(marketplace.json)에 반영되지 않음. 거짓은 아니나 불완전.

refutation.reason: Gate A passes: all three quotes are verbatim (marketplace.json:17, plugin.json:3, CHANGELOG.md:10). But the finding dies at Gate C — it is a completeness/taste trade-off, not an honesty defect. On axis 1 (정합·정직성) a defect requires a FALSE claim or a violated contract; there is neither. The finding itself concedes the point in reference_gap: '거짓은 아니나 불완전' (not false, but incomplete). The marketplace description is a true SUBSET of the plugin.json manifest, not a contradiction of it — every word ('select branching strategy … generate rules and auto-validate') is true. A marketplace one-liner omitting some features is universal and expected; no rule in CLAUDE.md requires marketplace.json to enumerate every feature or mirror plugin.json. Moreover the omission is INTENTIONAL and DOCUMENTED: CHANGELOG.md:10 records that v1.7.1 was a deliberate 'marketplace description 압축' (compression). The recommendation — expand the terse blurb to re-add charter — directly reverses a documented design decision and runs against devbrew's design-lightness convention. 'It would read more completely' is taste, not a defect. Discoverability is preserved because plugin.json/README carry the full feature set once a user clicks in.
facts: marketplace.json:17 verbatim: '"description": "Git workflow initialization: select branching strategy (GitHub Flow, Git Flow, Trunk-based), generate rules and auto-validate."' — citation accurate.

plugins/project-init/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:3 verbatim: '"description": "Initialize git-workflow rules and a project charter via a fact-routing interview, then generate agent-readable AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md docs with hook-based validation of branches, commits, doc conventions, and charter integrity."'; plugin.json:4 version is 1.7.2 — citation accurate.
CHANGELOG.md:8-10 verbatim: '## [1.7.2] — 2026-07-09' followed by '(v1.7.1은 marketplace description 압축에 따른 doc-only patch bump — 동작 변경 없음.)' — the compression was an intentional, documented decision.
The marketplace description contains no false statement; it is a true subset of the plugin.json manifest (no contradiction, only omission).
No rule in CLAUDE.md requires marketplace.json descriptions to enumerate all features or match plugin.json.

findings.title: 생성물 pr-process.md의 `/commit-push-pr` 권고가 의존 플러그인 조건 표기 없이 사용자 프로젝트로 복제됨(같은 섹션 line 78은 '(설치 시)' 표기, line 77은 누락)
findings.user_harm: templates/shared/pr-process.md:77이 'commit-commands: /commit-push-pr 사용'을 권고하며, 이 파일은 Step 4d에서 사용자 프로젝트의 docs/git-workflow/pr-process.md로 그대로 복제된다(이 리포의 docs/git-workflow/pr-process.md:77이 그 복제 증거). commit-commands 플러그인을 설치하지 않은 사용자가 이 생성 문서를 읽고 `/commit-push-pr`을 실행하면 명령이 없어 예측 가능하게 실패한다. 바로 아래 line 78(quality-gates)은 '(설치 시)' 조건을 달았는데 line 77은 달지 않아, 유지보수자가 조건 표기의 필요성을 알면서도 한 줄에서만 빠뜨린 비일관이다.
findings.recommendation: templates/shared/pr-process.md:77에 line 78과 대칭인 '(설치 시)' 또는 'commit-commands 플러그인 필요' 조건 표기를 추가한다. 선택적으로 project-init README에 prerequisites/optional-integrations 명시.
findings.counter_argument: line 77은 이미 굵은 '**commit-commands**:' 헤더로 명령의 출처 플러그인을 명시한다 — 사려 깊은 독자는 `/commit-push-pr`이 commit-commands 소속임을 알고 설치 필요를 유추한다. project-init은 commit-commands 에이전트를 *dispatch*하지 않고 명령을 *추천*만 하므로 CLAUDE.md의 'dispatch하는 플러그인은 prerequisites에 리스트' 규칙의 문자적 대상이 아니다(silent coupling이 아니라 named coupling). commit-commands는 공식 플러그인이라 회복이 쉽고 harm은 경미하다.

evidence.quote: - **commit-commands**: 간소화된 PR 생성을 위해 `/commit-push-pr` 사용
- **quality-gates** (설치 시): `gh pr create`에 quality 파이프라인 자동 트리거
- **commit-commands**: 간소화된 PR 생성을 위해 `/commit-push-pr` 사용
> 간결한 git 작업을 위해 `/commit` 또는 `/commit-push-pr` (commit-commands 플러그인) 사용.

findings.fix_cost_rationale: 템플릿 한 줄에 조건 표기 추가. 단일 파일. 이미 복제된 사용자 프로젝트 문서는 소급 수정 불가지만 향후 생성물은 정정됨.
findings.reference_gap: CLAUDE.md 'Silent coupling은 버그' 정신 + 같은 섹션 line 78의 '(설치 시)' 조건 표기 컨벤션에 line 77이 불일치. 생성물로 복제되는 의존 표기 누락.

refutation.reason: Gate A passes: pr-process.md:77/:78 and the docs/ copy are verbatim-accurate, and project-init.md:231 is verbatim. But the finding dies at Gate B — the hole is already closed and no user harm survives. Line 77 is NOT silent coupling: it leads with the bolded '**commit-commands**:' header that explicitly names the source plugin, so a reader (human or agent) reading the line knows `/commit-push-pr` belongs to the commit-commands plugin and requires it. This is the established convention in this codebase — project-init.md:231 does the same, naming '(commit-commands 플러그인)' in parentheses. The worst outcome for a user without commit-commands is a self-explaining 'command not found' whose remedy the line itself points at (install commit-commands). The CLAUDE.md coupling rule the finding invokes ('...를 dispatch하는 플러그인은 README prerequisites에 리스트; Silent coupling은 버그') targets plugins that DISPATCH another plugin's agent — project-init merely RECOMMENDS a command in a generated template, it does not dispatch, so the rule does not literally apply. The line-77-vs-line-78 asymmetry is also semantically justified, not an inconsistency: line 78 (quality-gates) describes a PASSIVE auto-trigger where '(설치 시)' explains WHEN the automatic behavior fires; line 77 (commit-commands) describes a MANUAL command whose owning plugin is already named in the header. Both statements are true — no falsehood on the honesty axis.
facts: templates/shared/pr-process.md:77 verbatim: '- **commit-commands**: 간소화된 PR 생성을 위해 `/commit-push-pr` 사용' — the source plugin is named in the bolded line header.
templates/shared/pr-process.md:78 verbatim: '- **quality-gates** (설치 시): `gh pr create`에 quality 파이프라인 자동 트리거' — describes an automatic passive trigger, semantically distinct from a manual command.
docs/git-workflow/pr-process.md:77 is byte-identical to the template line 77 (confirms the template is copied into user projects verbatim).

commands/project-init.md:231 verbatim: '간결한 git 작업을 위해 `/commit` 또는 `/commit-push-pr` (commit-commands 플러그인) 사용.' — the established convention names the source plugin in parentheses; the coupling is named, not silent.
project-init recommends the command in a template rather than dispatching a commit-commands agent, so CLAUDE.md's dispatch-prerequisites rule does not literally apply.

findings.title: git-flow 브랜치 전략 템플릿의 산문이 자기모순 — '소문자+숫자+하이픈만 허용'이라 적고 두 문장 뒤 'dot 포함은 OK'라 함(형제 템플릿은 'dot' 포함 명시)
findings.user_harm: templates/git-flow/branch-strategy.md:34가 '소문자 + 숫자 + 하이픈만 허용'(dot 배제)이라 단언한 직후 '`release/v1.2.0`처럼 dot 포함은 OK'라 정정해 같은 줄에서 모순된다. 이 파일은 Git Flow 선택 시 사용자 프로젝트의 docs/git-workflow/branch-strategy.md로 복제된다. github-flow(:15)와 trunk-based(:16) 형제 템플릿은 '소문자 + 숫자 + 하이픈 + dot만 허용'으로 올바르게 적었다. 사용자는 dot이 허용되는지 순간 혼동한다. regex(`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]*`)가 진짜 소스이며 dot을 허용하므로 산문의 '하이픈만' 표현이 틀린 쪽이다.
findings.recommendation: templates/git-flow/branch-strategy.md:34의 '소문자 + 숫자 + 하이픈만 허용'을 형제 템플릿과 동일하게 '소문자 + 숫자 + 하이픈 + dot만 허용'으로 정정한다.
findings.counter_argument: 같은 줄이 즉시 'dot 포함은 OK (`v` 시작 → `[a-z0-9]` 통과, `1.2.0`은 `[a-z0-9.-]*` 통과)'로 상세히 자기정정하므로 오해가 지속되지 않는다. 권위 있는 소스인 ```regex``` 블록은 정확하고, hook은 산문이 아니라 그 regex를 런타임에 읽으므로 enforcement에는 영향이 없다(순수 표현상 nitpick).

evidence.quote: 소문자 + 숫자 + 하이픈만 허용. URL-friendly + case-insensitive 파일시스템 충돌 방지. `release/v1.2.0`처럼 dot 포함은 OK (`v` 시작 → `[a-z0-9]` 통과, `1.2.0`은 `[a-z0-9.-]*` 통과).
소문자 + 숫자 + 하이픈 + dot만 허용 (예: `feature/v1.2-fix`). URL-friendly + case-insensitive 파일시스템 충돌 방지 (예: macOS는 `feature/Foo`와 `feature/foo`를 같은 브랜치로 본다).

findings.fix_cost_rationale: 한 단어 추가('+ dot'). 단일 파일 국소 편집.
findings.reference_gap: regex(source of truth)는 dot 허용인데 같은 파일의 산문이 'dot 배제'를 먼저 단언 → 문서-내부 및 형제 템플릿 간 비일관.

refutation.reason: Gate A passes: git-flow/branch-strategy.md:34, github-flow:15, and trunk-based:16 are verbatim-accurate, and the regex at git-flow:31 (`^(feature|fix|release|hotfix)/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]*$`) does allow dots. But the finding dies at Gate C — read as a whole (which is the only honest reading), the git-flow sentence is TRUE and self-consistent, not self-contradictory. It uses a 'rule + explicit exception' rhetorical structure: '소문자 + 숫자 + 하이픈만 허용' (the 만/only there excludes uppercase/underscore, which is the actual point — URL-friendly, case-insensitive FS collisions) followed immediately IN THE SAME SENTENCE by '`release/v1.2.0`처럼 dot 포함은 OK' with a precise walk-through of how the string passes the regex. The net semantic content equals the siblings' '하이픈 + dot만 허용' — the git-flow version is if anything MORE informative because it explains WHY dots pass. This is a phrasing-style difference between sibling templates, which is pure taste; no rule requires the three templates to word the naming rule identically, and there is no false claim about the code (the regex source of truth is correct and the prose correctly affirms dots). The 'momentary confusion' the finding alleges self-resolves within the same sentence, and the finding concedes enforcement is unaffected because the hook reads the regex, not the prose — so nothing breaks (Gate B corroborates). 'Phrase it like the siblings' is a consistency preference, not a defect.
facts: git-flow/branch-strategy.md:31 regex verbatim: '^(feature|fix|release|hotfix)/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]*$' — dots ARE allowed by the character class [a-z0-9.-].

git-flow/branch-strategy.md:34 verbatim: '소문자 + 숫자 + 하이픈만 허용. URL-friendly + case-insensitive 파일시스템 충돌 방지. `release/v1.2.0`처럼 dot 포함은 OK (`v` 시작 → `[a-z0-9]` 통과, `1.2.0`은 `[a-z0-9.-]*` 통과).' — the same sentence explicitly affirms dots are allowed, resolving any tension internally.

github-flow/branch-strategy.md:15 verbatim: '소문자 + 숫자 + 하이픈 + dot만 허용 (예: `feature/v1.2-fix`). ...' and trunk-based/branch-strategy.md:16 identical wording — the siblings use a complete-enumeration phrasing while git-flow uses rule+exception; net meaning is the same.
The finding concedes and CHANGELOG.md:25 (v1.7.0 get_branch_pattern) confirms the hook reads the fenced regex block at runtime, not the prose — so the wording has zero enforcement impact.
Read as a complete sentence, the git-flow prose makes no false claim; the alleged 'self-contradiction' is a rule-then-exception structure that resolves within the same line.

findings.title: Commit validator silently skips the most common commit form: git commit -am (and -m"msg", --message=)
findings.user_harm: A user who runs `git commit -am "add thing"` (staging + message in one combined short flag — one of the most common git commit forms) receives NO Conventional-Commits advisory, even though the identical message via `git commit -m "add thing"` is flagged. README:63 advertises "커밋 메시지 포맷 자동 검증" and README:95 claims the hook "Conventional Commits 포맷을 지속적으로 강제", so the user reasonably believes their commits are checked. The advisory has a large, silent blind spot for the exact invocation many people use every day.
findings.recommendation: Broaden COMMIT_MSG_RE so combined short flags and attached values are matched, e.g. allow other short flags before the m (`-[a-zA-Z]*m`) and permit the value to abut the flag (`\s*` instead of `\s+` before the quote), plus a branch for `--message[= ]`. Add regression tests for `git commit -am "..."`, `git commit -m"..."`, and `git commit --message="..."` (test_post_tool_use.py currently tests only the `-m "..."` form). Keep it non-blocking.
findings.counter_argument: The hook is advisory and non-blocking, so even when it DOES fire it only prints a nudge — nothing is prevented either way, and the harm is a missing nudge, not a wrong outcome. Claude Code's own system prompt and the commit-commands plugin already shape commit messages, and `-am` is arguably a discouraged habit (it couples staging with committing). Broadening the regex risks false positives (e.g. matching a literal `-m` inside a path or an unrelated token), and devbrew's own philosophy (feedback_harness_lightness_trust_model) says convention nudges should trust the model rather than chase every syntactic form. So the maintainers could reasonably classify this as an accepted false-negative surface parallel to docs-lint's documented scope-outs.

evidence.quote: COMMIT_MSG_RE = re.compile(r"""git\s+commit\s+[^;|&]*-m\s+(['"])(.*?)\1""")
msg = _hook.validate_commit('git commit -m "add thing"')

findings.fix_cost_rationale: Single regex in one file plus a handful of new unittest cases. Slightly above trivial because the broadened pattern must be crafted to avoid false-positive matches (e.g. `-m` inside a path), so it needs its own regression tests — one file, new behavior + tests.
findings.reference_gap: test_post_tool_use.py exercises commit validation only through `git commit -m "..."` (line 191-196 and the compound-command tests at 283/304/321). No test uses `-am`, `-m"..."` (attached), or `--message=`, so the blind spot is entirely unlocked — a mutation removing commit validation for combined flags would stay GREEN.
findings.impact: Advertised commit-format validation silently does not fire on a top-frequency commit invocation; user is misled about coverage. Recoverable (advisory only), no data loss.

refutation.reason: Gate A passes — the regex at post-tool-use.py:24 is quoted verbatim and the three non-match claims are mechanically correct (`-am` has no `-m` substring; `-m"..."` lacks the required `\s+`; `--message=` has `-m` but is followed by `essage`, not whitespace). But Gate B fails: the hook is explicitly advisory/non-blocking (README:83, README:86) and always exits 0 — a validator that does not fire on a given syntactic form produces a MISSING NUDGE, not a wrong outcome. The commit proceeds identically whether or not the advisory prints; nothing a user relies on breaks, no data loss, no misdirection. The claimed harm 'user reasonably believes their commits are checked / is misled about coverage' is exactly the speculative-confusion category Gate B rejects ('could be confusing'). README:95's '지속적으로 강제' sits in the Law-3 Compounding section and means the hook fires on every Bash invocation (which it does), not that it matches every git syntax — so no claim is false about its own code (Gate C would also fail). Gate F reinforces: broadening this non-load-bearing convention nudge to chase every syntactic variant contradicts the repo's documented harness-lightness principle (feedback_harness_lightness_trust_model: determinism only for load-bearing security/correctness gates), and the recommendation itself concedes the pattern 'must be crafted to avoid false-positive matches (e.g. `-m` inside a path)' — injecting nagging false positives into an advisory that is supposed to be a gentle nudge is a cure worse than the disease.
facts: post-tool-use.py:24 verbatim: COMMIT_MSG_RE = re.compile(r"""git\s+commit\s+[^;|&]*-m\s+(['\"])(.*?)\1""") — matches the finding's evidence quote exactly.

Trace `git commit -am "add thing"`: after `git commit `, `[^;|&]*-m` cannot match because the substring `-m` (dash immediately followed by m) does not occur in `-am` — the only `-` is followed by `a`. NOT flagged. Confirmed.
Trace `git commit -m"add thing"`: `-m\s+` requires >=1 whitespace; `-m"` has none, so no match. NOT flagged. Confirmed.
Trace `git commit --message="add thing"`: `-m` occurs inside `--m` but is followed by `essage`, not `\s+`, so `-m\s+(['"])` fails. NOT flagged. Confirmed.
README:63 reads '브랜치 이름·커밋 메시지 포맷 자동 검증'; README:95 reads '...브랜치 명명과 Conventional Commits 포맷을 지속적으로 강제' — both cited quotes are accurate.
README:83 and README:86 explicitly label both hooks 'advisory, non-blocking'; README:83 describes the commit path with NO exhaustive-coverage promise.
main() always calls sys.exit(0) (post-tool-use.py:215); the hook only prints a systemMessage nudge — it blocks/prevents nothing.
HEREDOC form `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'..."` IS handled by HEREDOC_COMMIT_RE (post-tool-use.py:25-28); plain `-m "..."` handled by COMMIT_MSG_RE.

test_post_tool_use.py exercises commit validation only via `-m "..."` (lines 191, 194) and compound `checkout -b ... && git commit -m "..."` forms (lines 283, 302, 321); no test uses `-am`, attached `-m"..."`, or `--message=` — the reference-gap claim is accurate.

findings.title: Branch-name validator only matches checkout -b / switch -c; bare `git branch <name>`, `checkout -B`, `switch -C` are unchecked
findings.user_harm: A branch created with `git branch feature/Bad_Name` (bare create, no switch) or `git checkout -B Bad_Name` / `git switch -C Bad_Name` (force-create) receives no naming advisory, while the same name via `git checkout -b` would be flagged. The advisory's coverage is inconsistent across equivalent branch-creation forms, so a user who happens to create branches the un-covered way gets no naming feedback at all.
findings.recommendation: Extend BRANCH_CREATE_RE to also cover bare creation and the capital force forms without introducing false positives — e.g. add an alternation for `git branch` followed by a non-flag token (`git\s+branch\s+(?![-])(\S+)`, which excludes `git branch -d/-m/-a/--show-current`) and accept `-B`/`-C`. Add regression tests for each new form and a negative test proving `git branch -d feature/x` is NOT flagged.
findings.counter_argument: This is the weakest of the two coverage findings: bare `git branch <name>` creates a branch the user is not yet working on, so an immediate naming nudge is less useful, and `-B`/`-C` (force re-create) are niche. More importantly, naively broadening the regex to `git\s+branch\s+(\S+)` would capture flag tokens (`git branch -d feature/x` -> `-d`) and fire spurious warnings on rename/delete/list commands — the current narrowness is partly a deliberate false-positive guard. The hook is advisory and a mis-named branch is fully recoverable with one `git branch -m`, so the cost of the gap is near-zero. A maintainer could reasonably keep the regex narrow.

evidence.quote: BRANCH_CREATE_RE = re.compile(r"git\s+(?:checkout\s+-b|switch\s+-c)\s+(\S+)")
match = BRANCH_CREATE_RE.search(command)

findings.fix_cost_rationale: One targeted regex alternation in one file plus positive/negative unittest cases; the negative test (ensuring `git branch -d/-m` do not match) is the only subtlety.
findings.reference_gap: No test in test_post_tool_use.py exercises `git branch <name>`, `git checkout -B`, or `git switch -C`; DerivePrefixesTest / F2SuggestionTest only cover the `checkout -b`/`switch -c` paths. The uncovered creation forms are neither validated nor locked.

findings.title: S4(i) rewrites a divergent CLAUDE.md to a one-line pointer without migrating its content — deterministic user-content loss that contradicts the plugin's own "preserve in all states" invariant
findings.user_harm: A user who has an AGENTS.md (canonical) plus a separately hand-written CLAUDE.md containing Claude-specific instructions not present in AGENTS.md is in state S4. Running /project-init shows an advisory with two options; choosing option (i) rewrites CLAUDE.md to the single line `@AGENTS.md` while leaving AGENTS.md unchanged. The unique CLAUDE.md content is neither preserved in CLAUDE.md nor migrated into AGENTS.md — it is discarded. Because `@AGENTS.md` imports only AGENTS.md, that content also vanishes from the model's loaded context. There is no filesystem backup; recovery is possible only via git, which fails if the CLAUDE.md was uncommitted. Crucially, the tool's own spec (line 167) promises non-managed content is preserved in ALL states with a single named exception (S2a-d), so a user reading that promise reasonably believes option (i) is a safe reformat — the consent is obtained under a false safety guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Make the S4(i) action mirror the content-preserving S2a path: extract non-managed content from the divergent CLAUDE.md and merge it into AGENTS.md BEFORE rewriting CLAUDE.md to the pointer (so AGENTS.md is not left 'unchanged' when CLAUDE.md holds unique content). Alternatively, if S4(i) must remain a discard, (a) update the line-167 invariant to name S4(i) as a second explicit exception (so the spec stops lying), (b) require the S4 advisory to state verbatim that divergent CLAUDE.md content will be permanently discarded and recommend commit/backup first, and (c) add a contract-test lock in test_command_contract.py (which today locks only the S2a/AC21 prompt, not any S4 disclosure).
findings.counter_argument: S4 is an uncommon state (most repos have either CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, not a divergent pair), the destruction is gated behind an explicit two-option user choice (not silent), and project-init's entire domain is git repositories — so a committed CLAUDE.md is recoverable via `git checkout`. One could argue 'divergent CLAUDE.md when AGENTS.md is canonical' is by definition stale content the user intends to abandon, making the discard the desired behavior; and the AGENTS.md-canonical design (D5-confirmed correct) means consolidating on one file is the point. A reviewer could therefore rate this MEDIUM (gated + git-recoverable) rather than HIGH.

findings.title: No recoverability preflight (backup, or commit/stash check) before any wholesale overwrite of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md — the safety net is git-only, on files the plugin itself says agents truncate
findings.user_harm: Every destructive path (S2a migrate-and-replace, S4(i) rewrite, C-S2 in-place docs overwrite, git-workflow 'replace?' overwrite) mutates the user's primary context files with no filesystem backup step. The approval prompts obtain consent to the action but never instruct the user or agent to ensure recoverability first. The S2a path in particular reads the entire existing CLAUDE.md and re-writes it as AGENTS.md relying on the model to carry over every non-managed section; the plugin's own docs-lint rule warns that agents 'will likely truncate' files over 300 lines — the exact class of file being read-and-rewritten. If the model drops a section during that migration and the original CLAUDE.md was uncommitted, the content is unrecoverable. The whole recovery model rests on (a) the model migrating correctly and (b) the file having been committed to git.
findings.recommendation: Add a cheap preflight to Step 1 / Step 4c: before the first overwrite of any existing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, use the already-available Bash tool to either (i) copy the file to a timestamped backup (e.g. `CLAUDE.md.project-init.bak`) that is removed on success, or (ii) run `git status --porcelain CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md` and, if either has uncommitted content, warn 'commit or stash before proceeding'. This converts an irreversible operation into a recoverable one for the uncommitted-file window that git alone cannot cover.
findings.counter_argument: project-init's domain is git repositories, and git IS the canonical, zero-litter backup — writing `.bak` files pollutes the working tree and duplicates what git already provides for committed content. The S2a truncation risk is probabilistic (model-dependent), not a deterministic failure with fixed inputs, so under a strict burden-of-proof it is closer to a hardening suggestion than a proven defect; the CHANGELOG (line 15) records a real WS5 sandbox S2a run where hand-curated content was preserved intact. A reviewer could reasonably say 'trust the model + git' and rate this LOW or treat it as an open question.

refutation.reason: Gate A passes (line 27 and docs-lint.py:125 are verbatim, and Grep confirms no backup/git-status/stash/commit preflight exists anywhere in the plugin — the absence claim is accurate). But Gate B fails: there is no deterministic failure with fixed inputs. Every stated harm is conditioned on 'if the model drops a section during migration' (model-dependent, probabilistic) AND 'if the original CLAUDE.md was uncommitted' — the finding's own counter_argument concedes it is 'closer to a hardening suggestion than a proven defect.' There is no reproduction, and the single real S2a execution on record (CHANGELOG v1.7.2 line 15, WS5 sandbox re-run performing the S2a approval path on a real repo copy) PRESERVED the hand-curated content intact and migrated it correctly to AGENTS.md (AC15/AC16 green) — the only defect found there was the unrelated H1 title, not content loss. So the observed behavior contradicts the theorized harm. The docs-lint:125 truncation warning is a post-write advisory about output-file LENGTH, not a migration-completeness check; it does not detect dropped sections, and the harm it is invoked for additionally requires a >300-line CLAUDE.md — a narrow, speculative intersection. oq_answers.answer: Do NOT promote branch/commit validation to a BLOCKING PreToolUse. Keep the current PostToolUse advisory as the default. A genuine middle ground exists — a PreToolUse hook that emits a WARNING ONLY (never permissionDecision deny/ask) before `git checkout -b`/`switch -c`/`branch` runs — and it would modestly improve the branch-naming UX by warning before creation instead of suggesting a post-hoc rename. But that middle ground is optional polish, not a defect to fix: it adds a second hook on the Bash PreToolUse hot path and can fire noise on commands that ultimately fail, for a benefit (avoiding one recoverable `git branch -m`) that the existing advisory already makes cheap.
oq_answers.reason: The post-hoc limitation is REAL and verified: PostToolUse fires after the tool executes, so by the time validate_branch runs the badly-named branch already exists and the hook can only offer `git branch -m <prefix>/{name_part}` (post-tool-use.py:128) — a rename, not a prevention. Likewise a commit is already made. That fact is what motivates the OQ. However, three lines of evidence make a BLOCKING promotion the wrong call: (1) branch naming is a recoverable STYLE rule, not a safety/correctness gate — a wrong name costs one rename, versus the destructive/boundary operations that legitimately warrant PreToolUse deny/ask in the precedent corpus (gstack freeze denies out-of-boundary writes, careful ASKS at check-careful.sh:109; ECC path-safety fails closed on trust-root escape). (2) The maintainers already made exactly this call deliberately: CHANGELOG.md:40 records that runtime base-branch/merge enforcement (F4/F5) was 'harness lightness — trust the model'로 명시 defer, and README.md:83 documents the hook as advisory/non-blocking on purpose. (3) devbrew's own standing lesson (feedback_harness_lightness_trust_model) reserves deterministic guards for load-bearing security/accuracy gates, not convention nudges — and sibling precedent (oh-my-claudecode merge-readiness: 'v1 is advisory does not block') keeps convention checks advisory. So: the middle ground is real but not compelled; promoting to deny would over-enforce a style rule against the plugin's own declared design and philosophy. Recommendation: keep PostToolUse advisory; only if the team specifically wants to kill the rename-dance should they add a PreToolUse WARNING-ONLY variant, and even then never deny/ask.

(1) Destruction paths enumerated: all destruction is in the LLM-executed prose of commands/project-init.md; both hooks (post-tool-use.py, docs-lint.py) always exit 0 and never Write. CLAUDE.md-mutating paths: S1 create (safe), S2a migrate-and-replace (content preserved by migrating to AGENTS.md), S4(i) rewrite-to-pointer (content DISCARDED, AGENTS.md unchanged), plus C-S2 in-place docs overwrite and the git-workflow 'replace?' overwrite. (2) Prompt coverage is complete at the path level: S2 has the Step-1 migration prompt (L25-27, test-locked as AC21), S4 has its 4c advisory (L165), the git-workflow overwrite has the Step-1 '교체할까요?' prompt (L20-21), and C-S2 has the '업데이트할까요?' prompt (L85). No CLAUDE.md overwrite is unprompted. (3) BUT: there is ZERO filesystem backup on any path — recovery depends entirely on git; the S4(i) advisory text is neither specified nor test-locked and need not disclose that divergent CLAUDE.md content is permanently discarded; and S4(i) directly contradicts the L167 invariant that non-managed content is preserved in all states. So prompts cover the actions, but the S4(i) consent is obtained under a false preservation promise, and no backup exists to recover from either an S4(i) discard or an S2a migration truncation on an uncommitted file.
